# Investigation Summary

## Symptoms

### Injection attack burst from a single spoofed-browser IP against /catalog
**Description:** A ~210-request injection campaign hit CloudFront distribution d111111abcdef8.cloudfront.net (EEXAMPLE000001) from a single source IP 198.51.100.40 (US), spanning 19:09:29–19:19:02 UTC. The requests carried a legitimate-looking Safari browser User-Agent (Mozilla/5.0 (Macintosh; Intel Mac OS X 14_6) ... Version/18.0 Safari/605.1.15) — explaining the 'e2-injection-browser-ua' event label. Targets: 180 GET /catalog (SQLi/XSS/LFI/SSRF), 15 POST /cart, 15 GET /home. All 210 injection-signature requests were BLOCKED by WAF managed rule groups; none were allowed through.
**Time:** 2026-10-10T19:09:00Z - 2026-10-10T19:19:00Z

## Findings

No findings identified.

## Other Gaps

### CloudWatch WAF metrics required dropping the Region dimension
**Description:** The initial GetMetricData returned no datapoints because it included Region=CloudFront, a dimension these metrics do not carry in this account. Re-querying with only WebACL+Rule returned full data; resolved, not a true blind spot.
